topics.displayName: Ask him what he saw or heard

lines.text: Mark is sitting against the wall of the gas station, shivering and clutching his brown paper bag.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Noises. Last night, before, always. Banging down below in the boiler room. Like someone pounding to be heard and nobody listens.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Banging from where?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: From under the motel floorboards. Someone was trapped down there. Then last night, she came bursting out like a ghost from the ground.
He speaks in feverish bursts, but a chilling pattern emerges from his words.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: I believe you, Mark. Go on.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Yeah? Nobody ever believes me. Not even Frank.
He calms down a little, his eyes widening with vivid memory.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: When she ran past me toward the hedges, I stumbled and dropped my gin bottle on the curb. Smashed into a hundred pieces.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Right behind her came a tall shadow with clean clothes and shiny shoes. I hid behind the pump because the dark around that man has teeth.

topics.displayName: Cut him off, he doesn't sound reliable

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: I get it, Mark. Thanks.
My skepticism shows in my tone immediately.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Sure. Like everyone else. The crazy drunk talks, nobody cares until the shadows swallow them too.

topics.displayName: Ask what scares him at night

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: You don't sleep much, do you, Mark?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Sleep's for people the dark doesn't want. I keep watch instead.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Same shapes pass by every night. Most never look down at me. That's how I know which ones to be scared of: the ones that never look down.
He pulls his knees in tighter and stares past me, like something's still walking by right now.

topics.displayName: Ask him about that night again

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Broken glass... cheap gin... it all blurs together in my head. I don't remember anything.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: What about the tall shadow in clean clothes?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: What shadow? Leave me alone. You already made up your mind about me.
He curls up against the bricks and looks away. He won't say another word.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Footsteps going down into the boiler room... almost every night for weeks.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: And right after the girl screamed in the bushes?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: That part... my head went blank with fear. I ran. But that bottle wasn't in my hand when she died, I swear on my mother's grave.
His terror is genuine. His bottle was the weapon, but he wasn't the killer.

lines.speaker: Gabe
lines.text: Last night in town, Mark. Anything you didn't tell me?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Told you everything already. Nobody wrote it down, though, did they. Nobody ever does.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.text: Whatever you decide, detective... just don't let the quiet ones win because they talk nicer than me.
For a moment his eyes are perfectly clear. Then the shaking starts again, and he's just the drunk by the gas station once more.
